feedback.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=4\sqrt{x}-4x$ at  $(1,0)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4\sqrt{x}-4x.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\sqrt{x}-4x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{1/2}-4x) \\  & =2{x}^{-1/2}-4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=2(1)^{-1/2}-4=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(0) & =-2(x-1) \\ y & =-2x+2-0 \\ y & =-2x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2(0)+2=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $(0,2).$
